item.title: International Women’s Day event hopes to raise $10K for three local charities
item.description: A pair of Fort St. John friends are hoping to raise $10,000 for three charities by organizing an International Women's Day event on March 8th, 2026.

item.title: Police say threats made against schools in Coquitlam, B.C., for third straight day
item.description: COQUITLAM — Police in the Metro Vancouver community of Coquitlam say more threats have been made toward local schools, setting off safety protocols. Coquitlam RCMP did not say how many schools were targeted in the latest round of threats but has confirmed that authorities have received additional reports of alleged threats Friday. item.title: Family of woman killed in Mexico forced to create new Facebook campaign group after copyright infringement report
item.description: The ‘Justice for Kiara’ Facebook group - which has now been taken down - was started by Kiara Agnew’s family after she was killed in Mexico in 2023 and her boyfriend, Ryan Friesen, found not guilty of femicide. That verdict has since been overturned, with Friesen launching an appeal.

item.title: Inaugural youth hangout aims to create safe, welcoming space in ‘coolest living room in town’
item.description: The free 4You Youth Hangout event will take place on Saturday, February 7th from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m. at the Lido Theatre.

item.title: Fort St. John school to host first Go Kart Rodeo
item.description: Fort St. John's Dr. Kearney Middle School is to host a Go Kart Rodeo on May 29th, 2026, and is inviting other schools to participate.

item.title: ‘Remarkable’: Society credits quick healing of bear burned near Dawson Creek to salve
item.description: NanoTess' NanoSALV has helped Valkyrie the black bear to heal the burns on her face and paws inflicted near Dawson Creek, according to the Northern Lights Wildlife Society.

item.title: Fort St. John Hospital ER re-opens after overnight closure
item.description: The Fort St. John Hospital's emergency department has re-opened after a staffing-related closure overnight from February 6th to 7th.

item.title: Fort Nelson ER closes all day for ‘staffing challenges’
item.description: The Fort Nelson General Hospital emergency department has closed for the day on February 7th due to "staffing challenges."

item.description: Meteorologists say the position of the jet stream is to blame for bone-chilling cold in southern Ontario, while daily high temperature records fall in Western Canada.
